model.name: Purchase Order
model.purpose: Represent a buyer-issued commercial commitment to acquire specified goods or services, and govern the accept, change, cancel and fulfilment-obligation lifecycle that follows from that commitment.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the format-neutral semantics of a purchase order as a buyer-to-seller commitment document: identity and type, contracting and supporting parties, line-level items and quantities, requested delivery and payment terms, anticipated amounts, references to quote/contract/catalogue, and the response, change and cancellation events that determine whether a contract is concluded. Syntax bindings such as UBL XML, UN/EDIFACT ORDERS or Peppol BIS, and storage interfaces such as Git, MCP or MongoDB, are projections of these semantics rather than the model itself.
in_scope: Buyer-assigned order identity, seller sales-order alias, instance UUID and specification or profile identifiers
Order type classification including order, blanket, call-off, consignment and related UN/EDIFACT document-name codes as alignments
Buyer, seller, originator, invoicee, consignee, delivery party and freight-forwarder roles on the order
Order lines, item identifiers and names, ordered quantities and units, net prices and line amounts
Header and line delivery locations, requested delivery times, delivery terms and limited transport instructions
Allowances, charges, estimated tax, anticipated monetary totals and buyer accounting or invoice-matching references
References to quotation, contract or framework agreement, catalogue, project, originator requisition and additional attachments
Seller accept, reject, partial accept and accept-with-change responses; buyer-initiated change and cancellation
Electronic formation, signature, acknowledgement, retention and validation rules that apply to the order as a data message
out_of_scope: The quotation or offer document itself, which belongs to sibling model WM-ECO-021
Physical fulfilment execution, despatch advice, receipt advice and transport documents, except as referenced obligations contained in WM-ECO-024
Invoice, credit note, remittance and payment-initiation instruments
Catalogue authoring, punch-out session payloads and price-list maintenance
Pre-award tendering, contract-award notices and public-procurement procedure documents
Master data registries for legal entities, products, locations or tax identifiers
Seller-internal sales-order planning, allocation, manufacturing or warehouse-picking systems

boundary_notes.distinction: A quotation is a seller proposal that may be referenced as the basis for an order. The purchase order is the buyer's subsequent commitment document; Peppol and UBL treat quotation reference as optional on the Order, not as the Order itself.

The order contains the commercial fulfilment obligations (what, how much, where, when). Execution artefacts such as despatch advice, receipt advice and transport status belong outside this model and are linked from the contained obligation rather than modelled as the order.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Invoice and Peppol BIS Billing order reference
boundary_notes.distinction: An invoice may cite the buyer purchase-order number for matching, but invoicing, tax reporting as a tax document, and payment are downstream. Peppol states that TAX on an order is informative and does not affect the terms of trade.

A contract or framework agreement may supply terms that the order calls off. The order is not the contract master; Peppol allows an order to refer to a framework, otherwise the buyer's terms apply until the seller accepts.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Internal requisition or EDIFACT document-name 105 Purchase Order
boundary_notes.distinction: UN/EDIFACT code 105 denotes an internal enterprise purchase order used to initiate buying for production. UBL and Peppol treat the exchanged buyer-to-seller document as Order (alternative business term Purchase Order) with default code 220. Internal requisitions map to OriginatorDocumentReference rather than to this model's exchanged commitment.
SalesOrderID is a seller-assigned alias. The authoritative identity of this model is the buyer's order number. Treating the sales order as the purchase order collapses two master systems.

sources.title: Universal Business Language Version 2.4
sources.relevance: Normative UBL business objects and ordering collaboration: Order, Order Response, Order Response Simple, Order Change and Order Cancellation, party roles, item identification, pricing, fulfilment versus ordering, and digital signatures.

sources.title: UBL 2.4 os - UBL-Order-2.4 data model
sources.relevance: Atomic Order ABIEs and BBIEs: buyer-assigned ID and Purchase Order Number, UUID, issue date and time, type code, parties, quotation and contract references, delivery terms, payment means and terms, tax total, anticipated monetary total and mandatory OrderLine.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Ordering 3.3
sources.version_or_date: BIS Ordering 3.3; Peppol BIS version 3 November 2025 / DEV 2026-Q2 documentation
sources.relevance: European ordering process: scope, parties, accept/reject/change rules, contract conclusion on acceptance, order type codes 220/105/221/226/227, product identification, totals calculation, tax as estimate, and interoperability profile identifiers.

sources.title: Peppol Order transaction 3.7 (T01) syntax binding to UBL Order
sources.relevance: Mandatory and optional order elements used in operational Peppol exchange, including CustomizationID, ProfileID, order identifier, issue date and time, currency, buyer, seller and order lines, plus fatal business rules.

sources.title: UN/EDIFACT Message ORDERS — Purchase order message, Release 99B
sources.organization: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UN/CEFACT)
sources.relevance: Functional definition of the Purchase order message as details of goods or services ordered under conditions agreed between seller and buyer; header, detail and summary structure; message type ORDERS.

sources.title: UNCITRAL Digest of Case Law on the United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law
sources.relevance: CISG Part II formation: a purchase order may be an offer if sufficiently definite as to goods, quantity and price (art. 14); acceptance by statement or conduct (art. 18); silence is not in itself acceptance; contract is concluded when acceptance becomes effective (art. 23).

sources.title: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce with Guide to Enactment 1996, with additional article 5 bis as adopted in 1998
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law
sources.version_or_date: 1996 Model Law; article 5 bis 1998; UN publication 19-04970
sources.relevance: Legal recognition of EDI data messages, writing and signature functional equivalents, retention of data messages (art. 10), formation and validity of contracts by data message (art. 11), acknowledgement of receipt (art. 14), and time and place of dispatch and receipt (art. 15).

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 — Invoice OrderReference (BT-13)
sources.relevance: Downstream interoperability: an invoice cites the buyer-issued purchase order identifier; buyer reference or purchase-order reference is required for matching, which is not invoicing itself.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a purchase order is identified, typed and bound to a business process or specification profile, independently of message syntax.
bundles.rationale: UBL, Peppol and UN/EDIFACT all treat the buyer-assigned document number as the primary key of the exchanged order and then classify the document by type and process profile. Without these facts an agent cannot cite, match or validate the commitment.

layers.name: Document identity
layers.description: Buyer master-system order number, seller sales-order alias, instance UUID, copy indicator and human references.

findings.name: Master order identity
findings.description: The exchanged order has a sender-assigned identifier that UBL names Order.ID and alternatively Purchase Order Number or Order Number. Peppol requires cbc:ID as the transaction instance identifier used for later references. A seller may assign SalesOrderID. UBL also permits a UUID for the document instance and a copy indicator.

questions.text: What buyer master-system purchase-order number identifies this commitment for all later responses, changes, cancellations, despatches and invoices?
What seller-assigned sales-order identifier, if any, aliases this purchase order in the seller's system without replacing the buyer number?
What instance UUID distinguishes this document occurrence, and is the payload a copy rather than the original issued order?
How must subsequent invoices or fulfilment messages cite this order so that matching uses the buyer number rather than a seller or transport identifier?

data_elements.name: Buyer order identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier for the order assigned by the sender; UBL alternative terms Purchase Order Number and Order Number; Peppol cbc:ID.

data_elements.name: Seller sales-order identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier for the order assigned by the seller.

data_elements.name: Document instance UUID
data_elements.description: Universally unique identifier for an instance of the order document.

data_elements.name: Copy indicator
data_elements.description: Indicates whether the document is a copy (true) or not (false).

data_elements.name: Customer or buyer reference
data_elements.description: Supplementary buyer contact or department reference that Peppol also expects on the corresponding invoice.

artifacts.name: Issued purchase-order document
artifacts.description: The buyer-issued order instance that carries the master identifier, regardless of whether it is projected as UBL Order, Peppol T01 or UN/EDIFACT ORDERS.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the buyer's master-system purchase-order number as the artefact identifier; record UUID as instance key; never use issue date as identity.

layers.name: Type, profile and process binding
layers.description: Order type codes and the specification or profile that constrain content and choreography.

findings.name: Order type and process profile
findings.description: UBL OrderTypeCode signifies the type of order. Peppol enumerates Order (default, UN/EDIFACT 220), Consignment order, Blanket order, Call-off order and Purchase order (105, internal-enterprise sense), bound by CustomizationID and ProfileID. UN/EDIFACT ORDERS is the purchase-order message used nationally and internationally.

questions.text: Which order type code applies, and does it mean a buyer-to-seller order (220), an internal enterprise purchase order (105), a blanket order, a call-off, or a consignment order?
In this adoption, is Purchase Order the exchanged buyer-to-seller commitment (UBL Order) or an internal requisition that must not be sent as ORDERS 220?
Which specification identification and business-process profile bind the instance, and which additional elements become mandatory under that profile?
Is the order issued in a bilateral EDI agreement, a Peppol four-corner network, or another collaboration, and which choreography of response documents applies?

data_elements.name: Order type code
data_elements.description: Code signifying the type of order; Peppol examples include 220 Order, 105 Purchase Order, blanket, call-off and consignment.

data_elements.name: Specification identification
data_elements.description: Identifies the specification of content and rules; Peppol example urn:fdc:peppol.eu:poacc:trns:order:3.

data_elements.name: Business process type identifier
data_elements.description: Identifies the BII or Peppol profile; Peppol ordering example urn:fdc:peppol.eu:poacc:bis:ordering:3.

data_elements.name: Profile execution identifier
data_elements.description: Identifies an instance of executing a profile so all transactions in a collaboration can be associated.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Type and profile are coded metadata on the order instance. Their governing code lists and profile URNs are referenced standards, not a separate stored artefact type.

findings.name: Issue time and validity window
findings.description: UBL requires IssueDate assigned by the sender and permits IssueTime and ValidityPeriod. Peppol requires IssueDate and permits IssueTime. These are event times of issuance, not identifiers.

questions.text: When did the buyer issue this order, as an event timestamp distinct from when a gateway or agent later observed or ingested it?
For what period is the order valid as an offer, and what happens if the seller responds after that window?
How is the Peppol date-without-timezone issue date combined with optional issue time into an RFC 3339 event time with seconds and explicit offset for this Dimension?

data_elements.name: Order issue date
data_elements.description: Date assigned by the sender on which the document was issued; Peppol mandatory; UBL mandatory.

data_elements.name: Order issue time
data_elements.description: Time assigned by the buyer on which the order was issued.

data_elements.name: Validity period
data_elements.description: Period for which the order is valid as an offer.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: Time the Dimension observed or ingested the order, recorded separately from issue event time when they differ.

artifacts.name: Order issuance event record
artifacts.description: Audit record of issuance combining business event time with gateway observation or ingestion time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Key by buyer order identifier plus issuance event timestamp; do not use the date alone as identity.

bundles.name: Parties and authority
bundles.description: Who issues, receives and is bound by the order, including supporting logistics and invoicee roles and the legal effect of issuance and acceptance.
bundles.rationale: Peppol and UBL make buyer and seller mandatory and distinguish originator, invoicee, consignee, delivery party and freight forwarder. CISG and Peppol then determine whether the document is an offer and when it becomes a contract.

layers.name: Contracting and supporting parties
layers.description: Legal and operational parties named on the order.

findings.name: Buyer, seller and supporting roles
findings.description: Peppol defines Customer and Supplier as business partners, with Buyer and Seller mandatory on the order. Optional roles are Originator, Invoicee, Consignee and Delivery party. UBL also records FreightForwarderParty. Party identifiers may carry ICD or EAS scheme attributes.

questions.text: Who is the buyer legal person or organisation, and which party, endpoint and legal-registration identifiers identify that buyer?
Who is the seller legal person or organisation that is asked to supply, and which identifiers and contacts address that seller?
Which originator, invoicee, consignee, delivery party or freight forwarder, if any, differs from buyer or seller, and where do they sit in the delivery chain?
Which party owns the commercial commitment on the customer side when originator, buyer and invoicee are split across units?

data_elements.name: Buyer customer party
data_elements.description: Mandatory buyer: legal person or organisation acting on behalf of the customer who buys the goods or services.

data_elements.name: Seller supplier party
data_elements.description: Mandatory seller: legal person or organisation acting on behalf of the supplier who sells to the customer.

data_elements.name: Originator customer party
data_elements.description: Person or unit that initiates the order, often the end user.

data_elements.name: Accounting customer party (invoicee)
data_elements.description: Person or unit that receives the invoice on behalf of the customer.

data_elements.name: Consignee and delivery party
data_elements.description: Delivery location consignee and optional final delivery party to whom the consignee forwards goods.

data_elements.name: Freight forwarder party
data_elements.description: Freight forwarder or carrier associated with the order.

artifacts.name: Order party snapshot
artifacts.description: Embedded party, address, endpoint, legal-entity and contact snapshot carried on the order at issue time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify parties by the scheme-qualified party or endpoint identifier present on the order; do not rely on display name alone.

layers.name: Commitment and legal authority
layers.description: When the order is an offer, when acceptance concludes a contract, and who is authorised to bind the buyer.

findings.name: Legal effect of the order
findings.description: UBL describes ordering as the collaboration that creates a contractual obligation between seller and buyer. Peppol states that the order agreed upon by acceptance has the commercial and legal status of a contract, and that rejection leaves no residual obligations. CISG art. 14 requires a sufficiently definite proposal indicating goods, quantity and price and an intention to be bound; art. 18 says silence or inactivity is not in itself acceptance; art. 23 concludes the contract when acceptance becomes effective. Electronic orders are data messages capable of forming contracts under MLEC art. 11.

questions.text: Is this purchase order a sufficiently definite offer under the applicable formation law, including identifiable goods, quantity and price or a method to determine them?
Which formation regime governs (CISG Part II, domestic sale-of-goods law, public-procurement rules, or a trading-partner agreement) and have any writing-requirement reservations been declared?
Who is authorised to issue or amend the order so that the buyer is bound, and how is that authority evidenced?
Must the seller accept expressly, may conduct such as despatch constitute acceptance, and is silent non-response ever treated as acceptance under an established practice?

data_elements.name: Governing formation regime
data_elements.description: Law or agreement under which the order is an offer and acceptance concludes a contract.

data_elements.name: Intention to be bound
data_elements.description: Indicator or evidence that the buyer intends to be bound if the seller accepts, as required for an offer.

data_elements.name: Authorised issuer
data_elements.description: Person or system authorised to issue the order on behalf of the buyer.

data_elements.name: Transaction conditions
data_elements.description: Purchasing or sales conditions applying to the whole order.

artifacts.name: Authority and formation evidence
artifacts.description: Signature, trading-partner agreement clause, or procurement mandate that shows who may bind the buyer and under which formation rules.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Link evidence to the buyer order identifier and the authorised-issuer identity; retain as part of the data-message original.

bundles.name: Line composition and fulfilment obligations
bundles.description: What is ordered, in what quantity, under which item identity, and which fulfilment obligations the order contains.
bundles.rationale: UBL requires one or more OrderLines; Peppol requires each line to have an item identifier and/or name and a quantity with unit. Those lines are the contained fulfilment obligations of WM-ECO-024 rather than execution documents.

layers.name: Lines, items and quantities
layers.description: Line structure, item identification systems and ordered quantities.

findings.name: Order line and item
findings.description: UBL distinguishes LineItem as the line structure from Item as the generic item of sale. Peppol requires Sellers ID and/or Standard ID such as GTIN, and/or an item name, with Quantity and unitCode. Free-text articles and services are in-scope use cases. Prices may be omitted when unknown, forcing a detailed seller response.

questions.text: Which order lines constitute this commitment, and what line identifiers allow invoice and despatch line matching?
For each line, which seller, buyer, manufacturer, catalogue or standard item identifier and item name identify the goods or service?
What quantity and unit of measure are ordered on each line, and is the price base quantity different from the order quantity?
If the item is free text or a service without a catalogue number, what description, attributes or period are required so the seller can identify what to supply?

data_elements.name: Order line
data_elements.description: A line specifying a kind of item being ordered; UBL cardinality 1..n; Peppol cac:OrderLine mandatory.

data_elements.name: Line identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the order line used for later order-line references on invoices and fulfilment documents.

data_elements.name: Item identifiers
data_elements.description: Seller, buyer, manufacturer, catalogue or standard identifiers, including GTIN as StandardItemIdentification.

data_elements.name: Item name and description
data_elements.description: Product name and optional description on the line item.

data_elements.name: Ordered quantity
data_elements.description: Quantity ordered with a unit of measure code.

artifacts.name: Order line list
artifacts.description: The ordered set of lines that is the commercial payload of the purchase order.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify each line by buyer order identifier plus line identifier; do not identify a line by item name alone.

layers.name: Contained fulfilment obligations
layers.description: The order contains fulfilment obligations; it does not execute logistics.

findings.name: Fulfilment obligation set
findings.description: Each accepted order line is a fulfilment obligation: supply the identified item in the ordered quantity to the named place in the requested time. UBL keeps hazardous-item transport detail and actual consignments out of the order stage. Split, intermediary and consolidated fulfilment are shipment/consignment concerns, not order identity.

questions.text: Which fulfilment obligations does this order contain, and how does each map to an order line rather than to a later despatch?
May the seller substitute items or split deliveries, and did the buyer mark potential acceptable alternatives?
How is each obligation linked to sibling fulfilment execution without treating despatch advice as part of the purchase order?

data_elements.name: Fulfilment obligation references
data_elements.description: Contained obligations derived from accepted order lines, pointing at WM-ECO-024 instances.

data_elements.name: Acceptable alternatives indicator
data_elements.description: Buyer indication of potential acceptable alternatives on the order.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Fulfilment obligations are derived references from order lines into sibling model WM-ECO-024. The order document is the parent artefact; the obligation set is not a second serial document type at this layer.

bundles.name: Commercial, delivery and settlement terms
bundles.description: Prices, allowances, estimated tax, anticipated totals, delivery terms and locations, payment terms and buyer accounting strings.
bundles.rationale: Peppol and UBL specify how amounts are calculated and that tax on an order is an estimate. Delivery and payment terms on the order are requested commercial conditions, not proof of delivery or payment.

layers.name: Prices, tax and totals
layers.description: Net prices, allowances and charges, estimated tax and anticipated monetary totals.

findings.name: Monetary totals and tax estimates
findings.description: Peppol requires document currency and defines LineExtensionAmount, AllowanceTotalAmount, ChargeTotalAmount and related anticipated totals. Prices should include allowances or charges but exclude TAX. TAX on orders is an estimate to aid matching and must not be treated as a tax return. UBL requires senders to manifest calculated values so receivers need not recompute.

questions.text: What document, pricing, tax and requested-invoice currencies apply, and which net unit prices and price base quantities are stated?
Which header and line allowances or charges apply, including charge indicator, reason, base amount, percentage and amount?
What anticipated line-extension, allowance, charge, tax-exclusive, tax-inclusive and payable totals did the buyer manifest, and do they satisfy the Peppol calculation rules?
Is stated TAX only an estimate for matching, and which buyer TAX number is supplied for reverse-charge or similar invoice reporting?

data_elements.name: Document currency
data_elements.description: Default currency for the order; mandatory in Peppol.

data_elements.name: Price
data_elements.description: Net unit price excluding TAX, optionally with base quantity and a single price-level allowance.

data_elements.name: Allowance or charge
data_elements.description: Header or line allowance or charge with ChargeIndicator, reason, amount and optional tax category.

data_elements.name: Tax total
data_elements.description: Specification of expected tax amount; Peppol treats it as informative.

data_elements.name: Anticipated monetary total
data_elements.description: Total amount for the order anticipated by the buyer, including line extension, allowances, charges and payable amount.

artifacts.name: Anticipated totals breakdown
artifacts.description: Manifest monetary calculation carried on the order so a receiver need not recompute.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Attach to the buyer order identifier; version with any order change that alters amounts.

layers.name: Delivery, payment and accounting
layers.description: Requested delivery terms and locations, expected payment means and terms, and buyer accounting strings.

findings.name: Delivery terms and locations
findings.description: Peppol gives limited transport support: requested delivery location, basic term, time and contacts. UBL Order has Delivery and DeliveryTerms; delivery terms include Incoterms-style conditions such as CIF, FOB or EXW as alignments, not as claimed ICC conformance. Header delivery terms may be refined on lines.

questions.text: Where should the seller deliver, including consignee location and any final delivery party, and how does that differ from the buyer postal address?
What requested delivery date, period or time window applies at header or line, as event times rather than identifiers?
Which delivery terms or Incoterms-style code and special delivery instructions apply, and who pays freight or documentation charges?

data_elements.name: Delivery information
data_elements.description: Requested delivery location, party and period.

data_elements.name: Delivery terms
data_elements.description: Set of delivery terms associated with the order, including Incoterms-style codes as alignment.

data_elements.name: Delivery contact
data_elements.description: Contact person for delivery of the order.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Delivery instructions are structured fields on the order and optional address snapshots. They are not a bill of lading or despatch advice; those remain out of scope.

findings.name: Payment terms and accounting codes
findings.description: UBL records expected PaymentMeans, PaymentTerms, AccountingCost and AccountingCostCode. Peppol uses AccountingCost and CustomerReference so the seller can repeat them on the invoice. The order may be on account, card or direct debit; this is not payment execution.

questions.text: What payment terms and expected means of payment does the buyer request on this order?
What buyer accounting cost string or code must the seller repeat on the invoice for automated booking?
If invoicee differs from buyer, which invoicee party must appear on later invoices, and how does that relate to Peppol Billing buyer reference rules?

data_elements.name: Payment terms
data_elements.description: Payment terms associated with the order.

data_elements.name: Payment means
data_elements.description: Expected means of payment.

data_elements.name: Buyer accounting cost
data_elements.description: Buyer accounting cost centre or string to be repeated on the invoice.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Payment and accounting terms are inline commercial fields on the order used for later invoice matching. They are not remittance-advice or payment-initiation artefacts.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, response and exceptions
bundles.description: Seller response, contract conclusion, buyer change and cancellation, and special patterns such as blanket, call-off, consignment and vendor-managed inventory.
bundles.rationale: UBL and Peppol define a choreography in which an order is not a finished contract until accepted, may be replaced by a full Order Response or Order Change, and may be cancelled subject to contract. Rare types and VMI are documented in the same sources and must not be treated as canonical for every adoption.

layers.name: Seller response and contract conclusion
layers.description: Accept, reject, partial accept and accept-with-change.

findings.name: Seller response lifecycle
findings.description: Peppol allows the seller to accept in full, reject entirely, accept partially, or accept with changes only if a prior agreement defines how buyer assent to the change is established. Several responses may exist for one order; one response refers to one order. UBL Order Response Simple confirms without change or rejects; the full Order Response proposes to replace the original order and may supply missing dates, prices, discounts, charges or classifications. Rejection after receipt of a rejecting response lets the buyer start a new ordering process.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle state of this order: issued, received, accepted, accepted-with-change, partially accepted, rejected, replaced, or cancelled?
When and how did the seller respond, including response code, reasons for rejection, and whether the response replaces the entire order or only some lines?
Has a contract been concluded by effective acceptance, and at what event time did that acceptance reach the buyer?
If multiple or partial responses exist, which lines remain open, which are accepted, and which require a new buyer order?

data_elements.name: Order lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Current state derived from issued order plus subsequent response, change and cancellation documents.

data_elements.name: Seller response code
data_elements.description: Code indicating accept, reject, or accept with change at document or line level.

data_elements.name: Contract concluded indicator
data_elements.description: Whether acceptance has given the order the commercial and legal status of a contract.

data_elements.name: Acceptance effective time
data_elements.description: Event time at which acceptance became effective; record separately from ingestion time.

artifacts.name: Order response document
artifacts.description: Seller response that accepts, rejects or proposes a replacement state of the order.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by seller response identifier plus referenced buyer order identifier; one response refers to one order.

layers.name: Change, cancellation and special patterns
layers.description: Buyer amendments and uncommon but sourced order types.

findings.name: Buyer change and cancellation
findings.description: UBL allows the buyer to change an established order by Order Change, which reflects the entire current state, or by Order Cancellation followed by a replacement Order. Sellers accept or reject a change with Order Response or Order Response Simple. Cancellation may be ignored at manufacture or delivery initiation depending on contract; it may or may not be automated. CISG art. 29 treats modification proposals under the same offer-acceptance paradigm.

questions.text: What buyer change is in force, does it replace the entire previous order state, and has the seller accepted that change?
Has the buyer issued a cancellation, at what event time, and do contract terms still require fulfilment because manufacture or delivery has begun?
Who has authority to change or cancel, and which trading-partner or public-procurement rules limit cancellation after acceptance?

data_elements.name: Order change reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a buyer Order Change that states the entire current order transaction.

data_elements.name: Order cancellation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a buyer Order Cancellation document.

data_elements.name: Cancellation honoured indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the cancellation took effect or was ignored under contract at manufacture or delivery initiation.

artifacts.name: Order change document
artifacts.description: Buyer document stating the entire current state of an established order.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by change-document identifier plus original buyer order identifier; the change artefact replaces prior state only after seller acceptance where required.

artifacts.name: Order cancellation document
artifacts.description: Buyer document cancelling an established order transaction.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by cancellation-document identifier plus original buyer order identifier.

findings.name: Blanket, call-off, consignment and VMI patterns
findings.description: Peppol documents blanket, call-off and consignment (type 227) orders, including vendor-managed inventory where withdrawal of stock auto-issues a consignment order. UBL describes VMI, cyclic replenishment and replenishment on customer demand as related processes that may use Order plus catalogue, despatch and inventory documents. These patterns are in the wide-union surface but are not default for every adoption.

questions.text: Is this a standalone order, a blanket, a call-off against a blanket or contract, a consignment or VMI withdrawal, or a rush or standing order?
If this is a call-off, which blanket quantities, dates and locations does it split, and what remaining blanket balance is left?
If this is a VMI or consignment order, was it issued automatically on withdrawal, and does the seller still send an order response acknowledgement without treating it as a new offer negotiation?

data_elements.name: Order pattern code
data_elements.description: Classification of standalone, blanket, call-off, consignment, VMI or related pattern.

data_elements.name: Prior order or blanket reference
data_elements.description: Reference to another order, used for call-off or replacement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Blanket, call-off and VMI are classification and process patterns over the same order document type. They do not introduce a separate serial artefact beyond the issued order and its response.

bundles.name: Evidence, governance and interoperability
bundles.description: Related-document graph, signatures and attachments, validation quality, access, privacy, retention and cross-standard alignment.
bundles.rationale: Orders cite quotations, contracts, catalogues, originator requisitions and invoices; they may carry signatures and binary attachments; Peppol and UBL impose fatal validation rules; MLEC governs retention of the data message.

layers.name: Related documents and provenance
layers.description: Quotation, contract, catalogue, project, originator and additional document references.

findings.name: Related document graph
findings.description: UBL Order may reference a Quotation, other Orders, an Originator document, a Catalogue, additional documents, Contracts and Projects. Peppol uses these to ground the order in a prior quote, framework or internal requisition. Invoice matching later uses the buyer order id (BT-13) or buyer reference.

questions.text: Which quotation, contract or framework, catalogue and project identifiers is this order based on?
Which originator or internal requisition document caused this order to be issued?
How does this order reference WM-ECO-021 quotes and contain WM-ECO-024 fulfilment obligations without duplicating those models?

data_elements.name: Quotation document reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a quotation which is the basis for the order.

data_elements.name: Contract reference
data_elements.description: Contracts associated with the order, including framework agreements.

data_elements.name: Catalogue reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the catalogue on which the order is based.

data_elements.name: Originator document reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a document that originated the order, such as an internal requisition.

data_elements.name: Additional document reference
data_elements.description: Reference to additional documents, including attached drawings or other files.

artifacts.name: Related-document reference set
artifacts.description: The set of external document identifiers cited by the order.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each reference uses the cited document's own master identifier and document type; it is not a copy of that document.

layers.name: Integrity, validation, access and retention
layers.description: Signatures, attachments, schema and business-rule validation, access control, personal data and retention of the data message.

findings.name: Signatures, attachments and validation
findings.description: UBL supports enveloped XML digital signatures and XAdES. Peppol permits Base64 attachments or URI links and recommends embedded objects; attachments are additional information, not order copies. Peppol fatal rules require CustomizationID, ProfileID, ID, IssueDate, DocumentCurrencyCode, Buyer, Seller and OrderLine, and forbid extra elements and schemaLocation. UBL conformance is XSD plus additional document constraints; senders must manifest all calculated values.

questions.text: Is the order signed, with which signature profile, and what integrity hash binds the signature to the issued content?
Which additional binary or URI attachments accompany the order, and are they supporting drawings rather than a second copy of the order?
Which XSD, Schematron and profile business rules were applied, and did the instance pass the fatal Peppol and UBL constraints?
Are all fixed and calculated amounts manifested by the sender so the receiver is not required to recompute the calculation model?

data_elements.name: Document signature
data_elements.description: A signature applied to the order document.

data_elements.name: Embedded or referenced attachment
data_elements.description: Binary object or external URI supporting the order, with mime code and filename.

data_elements.name: Validation result
data_elements.description: Outcome of XSD and business-rule validation against the applicable profile.

artifacts.name: Signed order instance
artifacts.description: Order payload plus optional enveloped or detached signature.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by buyer order number and document UUID; integrity is the signature digest over the canonical payload.

artifacts.name: Validation report
artifacts.description: Machine report of schema and Schematron evaluation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by validated document UUID plus validator profile identifier and validation event time.

findings.name: Access, privacy and retention
findings.description: Orders contain party contacts, employee names, emails, telephone numbers and buyer references. MLEC art. 10 requires retention of data messages in a form that can be accessed and that preserves integrity, with origin and destination and time of dispatch and receipt. Peppol notes eSignature validation is not mandatory in the Ordering BIS. Access is restricted to the trading parties, their processors and auditors. Deletion of the commercial record is not the same as business cancellation.

questions.text: Which parties, processors and auditors may read this order, and which fields are restricted to finance or legal roles?
Which contact names, employee identifiers, emails or phone numbers on the order are personal data, and what processing purpose justifies their retention?
How long must the original order data message be retained in accessible, integrity-preserving form, and when may it be deleted or anonymised without erasing the commercial cancellation history?
What exception process applies if a party needs a copy after access expiry, or if a signature was not used because Peppol Ordering does not mandate eSignature?

data_elements.name: Access scope
data_elements.description: Parties and roles permitted to read or act on the order.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration for which the data message must remain accessible and integrity-checked.

data_elements.name: Dispatch and receipt times
data_elements.description: Time and place of dispatch and receipt of the data message, retained with the original.

artifacts.name: Retained original data message
artifacts.description: Accessible, integrity-preserving original of the order message including origin, destination and dispatch or receipt times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Retain under the buyer master-system order number plus message interchange identifier; record dispatch and receipt event times separately from ingestion into the archive.

functions.name: Issue purchase order
functions.description: Buyer creates and sends an order that specifies goods or services under conditions known to the buyer, assigning a master order number and issue event time.
inputs: order lines with item identity or name and quantities
optional quote, contract or catalogue references
outputs: issued order document with buyer order identifier
preconditions: Buyer is authorised to bind the customer
Goods or services, quantity and price are indicated or determinable if the order is to operate as an offer
Seller electronic address or EDI endpoint is known where electronic exchange is used
effects: Creates a buyer commitment document that is an offer or a call-off under an existing contract
Makes the buyer order number the reference key for later response, fulfilment and invoice matching

functions.name: Respond to purchase order
functions.description: Seller accepts in full, rejects, accepts partially, or accepts with changes where a prior agreement allows, using Order Response Simple or full Order Response.
inputs: optional replacement lines, prices, dates or classifications
preconditions: Accept-with-change is used only if a prior contract defines how buyer assent to changes is established
effects: On full acceptance, the order gains the commercial and legal status of a contract
On rejection, no contract and no residual obligations exist
On replacement response, the response reflects the entire new state of the order transaction

functions.name: Change purchase order
functions.description: Buyer issues an Order Change that states the entire current order, or cancels and issues a replacement Order; seller accepts or rejects the change.
inputs: changed lines, quantities, dates or addresses
preconditions: Legal contract or trading-partner agreement permits the change method used
effects: Replaces the current order state if and when the seller accepts
Does not silently patch history; prior issued content remains as provenance

functions.name: Cancel purchase order
functions.description: Buyer issues an Order Cancellation. Effect depends on contract; cancellation may be ignored once manufacture or delivery has begun.
preconditions: Authority and timing satisfy the applicable contract or procurement rules
effects: If honoured, remaining fulfilment obligations cease
If ignored, residual obligations continue and the cancellation remains as an event record rather than a delete

functions.name: Calculate anticipated totals
functions.description: Sender computes and manifests line extension, header allowances and charges and anticipated payable amounts using the Peppol formulae, without requiring the receiver to recompute.
preconditions: Line amounts are present when totals are stated
effects: Places all calculated values in the instance so a receiver print or matching process need not know the calculation model

functions.name: Validate order instance
functions.description: Evaluate the instance against the applicable UBL schema, additional UBL document constraints and, where used, Peppol fatal business rules.
preconditions: Profile and customization identifiers, when required by the network, are present
effects: Blocks non-conformant instances from being treated as Peppol or UBL conforming orders
Does not by itself create legal conformance claims beyond the rules actually evaluated

functions.name: Conclude contract on acceptance
functions.description: Record that an acceptance has become effective, distinguishing CISG reach-the-offeror timing from MLEC dispatch and receipt of the data message.
inputs: issued order that is an offer
seller acceptance statement or qualifying conduct
outputs: dispatch and receipt times of the acceptance message
preconditions: Order was a sufficiently definite offer or a call-off under an existing contract
Acceptance indicates assent and is not a material counter-offer unless treated as a new offer
effects: Creates the contractual obligation described by UBL ordering and Peppol acceptance
Leaves a rejected order without residual obligations

composition.purpose: The accepted order contains line-level fulfilment obligations for what, how much, where and when to supply; execution documents remain outside this model.
A purchase order may originate from an accepted quotation via QuotationDocumentReference; the quote is not the order.
Registered parent of this standalone purchase-order aggregate in the economic-order navigation path.

composition.target: OASIS UBL 2.4 Order and ordering collaboration
composition.purpose: Align identity, parties, lines, response, change and cancellation semantics to UBL Order, Order Response, Order Change and Order Cancellation without claiming XML conformance unless validated.

composition.target: Peppol BIS Ordering 3.3 and Order transaction T01
composition.purpose: Align European public and B2B ordering choreography, mandatory elements, type codes and totals rules to Peppol Ordering.
Align the functional definition of a purchase-order message and document-name codes such as 220 Order and 105 internal Purchase Order.
Align offer, acceptance, silence and conclusion-of-contract rules for international sales of goods; do not claim CISG always governs services or domestic orders.

composition.target: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce
composition.purpose: Align electronic formation, signature functional equivalent, acknowledgement, dispatch and receipt times, and retention of the order as a data message.

composition.target: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 invoice order reference
composition.purpose: Downstream invoices cite the buyer purchase-order identifier for matching; invoicing remains a sibling concern.
Orders may be based on a catalogue or call off a framework contract without absorbing those masters.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the adopting organisation that acts as records controller for issued and received purchase orders
Declare the buyer master order-management or ERP system that mints Order.ID values
Declare the applicable formation law or trading-partner agreement and whether CISG Part II applies
Declare the exchange network or profile (for example Peppol ordering, bilateral EDIFACT, or internal-only)
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-owned IRI namespace under the economic-order path NAV.SOC.ECO.ORD for governed identifiers, and keep buyer master-system order numbers as the first identity; do not mint identifiers from issue dates.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical order state is the latest seller-accepted full state: original Order, or accepted Order Response replacement, or accepted Order Change
Buyer order number is invariant across change and cancellation; new orders after rejection receive new buyer numbers
Amounts and quantities are stored as manifested by the sender; receivers do not recompute missing totals
Party snapshots on the order are canonical for that issuance even if later master data changes
patch_rules: Do not patch an issued order in place to change commercial content; issue Order Change or Cancellation plus replacement Order
Technical corrections of transmission copies may set CopyIndicator without changing Order.ID
Profile or customization identifiers may be added only when they do not alter already accepted commercial terms
compatibility_rules: UBL minor-version backward compatibility is an alignment, not automatic Dimension conformance
Peppol fatal extra-element rules are stricter than UBL extensibility; a UBL-valid extension may still fail Peppol
EDIFACT ORDERS and UBL Order are semantically aligned, not bit-compatible
ISO/IEC 19845 freeze versions lag OASIS UBL 2.4 and must be recorded as the alignment target actually used

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the buyer's purchase-order number as assigned by the buyer's order-management or ERP system (UBL Order.ID, Peppol cbc:ID, UN/EDIFACT BGM document number)
Governed global identifier or IRI assigned by an adopting network or this Dimension when one exists
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system or governed global identifier is available (UBL Order.UUID)
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record each business event time (issue, acceptance, change, cancellation, dispatch, receipt) and, when it differs, the observation or ingestion time as separate RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; never treat a date as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts are named {buyer-order-id}[--{role}][--{sequence}] where role is order, response, change or cancellation and sequence increments for multiple responses; do not embed calendar dates in the identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Preserve the original data message so that content is accessible and unaltered, with origin, destination and dispatch or receipt times; when signed, bind integrity to the signature digest over the canonical payload.

policies: Treat silent non-response as non-acceptance unless a proven practice or usage to the contrary is recorded for those parties
Accept-with-change is forbidden unless a prior agreement defines how buyer assent to the change is obtained
Tax figures on an order are estimates and must not be filed as a tax return from this model
Cancellation is a new event document; it is not physical deletion of the retained original
Personal contact data on the order is collected only for ordering, delivery and invoice-matching purposes

read: Buyer, seller and authorised processors may read orders they issued or received
Auditors and regulators may read under the recorded access scope
Supporting parties may read only fields needed for their role (consignee sees delivery, invoicee sees accounting references)
create: Only the buyer or an authorised originator system may create an issued order with a new buyer order number
Seller systems create response artefacts, not the purchase order itself
update: Commercial updates occur only via Order Change or replacement Order after cancellation, plus seller response
Lifecycle state and validation reports may be appended without rewriting issued content
delete: Do not delete retained originals during the retention period
Business cancellation does not authorise destruction of the data message
After retention expiry, deletion or anonymisation must preserve a non-personal audit stub of identifiers and event times

roles.name: Buyer
responsibilities: Issue, change and cancel purchase orders
State requested delivery, payment and accounting references

roles.name: Seller
responsibilities: Supply missing prices, dates or item classifications in a full response

roles.name: Originator
responsibilities: Initiate demand through a requisition or originator document
May become buyer when placing the order

roles.name: Invoicee
responsibilities: Receive invoices that must match the order references
Supply invoice-matching keys to be copied by the seller

roles.name: Consignee or delivery party
responsibilities: Receive goods at the stated location
Do not alter commercial order terms

roles.name: Dimension records steward
responsibilities: Enforce identity priority, timestamp rules, access scopes and retention of originals
Prevent silent patches and date-as-identifier usage

access.default_rule: Need-to-know among the contracting parties and their authorised processors; default deny to all other subjects.
exceptions: Regulators or courts may compel disclosure of retained originals
A consignee may be given delivery fields without price or allowance detail
Unsigned Peppol orders remain valid under the Ordering BIS, which does not mandate eSignature
audit_requirements: Log issue, dispatch, receipt, validation, response, change, cancellation, access and deletion events with RFC 3339 event time and separate ingestion time when they differ
Retain originator, addressee and message identifiers with the original data message

coverage.claim: This model is a defensible, format-neutral account of the buyer-issued purchase order as a commercial commitment and of the UBL, Peppol, UN/EDIFACT and CISG-aligned accept, change and cancel lifecycle. It is not a claim of universal legal completeness or of syntactic conformance to any one binding.

checklist.notes: Buyer master-system order number is primary; seller sales-order id, UUID, Peppol cbc:ID and EDIFACT BGM number are aligned aliases or instance keys.
Issue, validity, accept, reject, partial accept, accept-with-change, replace, change and cancel are sourced from UBL and Peppol; post-manufacture cancellation ignore is included.
Buyer, seller and supporting parties; quote, contract, catalogue, project, originator, invoice and fulfilment-obligation links.
Issue date and time, validity period, requested delivery, acceptance effective time, and MLEC dispatch and receipt times; event time separated from ingestion.
Originator document, quotation basis, copy indicator, signature, interchange identifiers and retained original data message.
Buyer owns the commitment; split originator, buyer and invoicee is modelled; seller owns the sales-order alias only.
UBL XSD plus additional constraints; Peppol fatal business rules; manifested totals; profile identifiers.
Need-to-know among parties and processors; role-scoped fields; audit of access exceptions.
MLEC art. 10 retention of accessible, integrity-preserving data messages; cancellation is not deletion; post-retention anonymisation of contacts.
Alignments to UBL 2.4, Peppol Ordering T01, UN/EDIFACT ORDERS, CISG Part II, MLEC and Peppol Billing order reference, with explicit non-conformance caveats.
Delivery location, consignee, delivery party and Incoterms-style delivery terms as order instructions, not transport documents.
Offer definiteness, authorised issuer, acceptance methods and public-procurement legal interoperability noted by Peppol.
Quantities with units, net prices, allowances, charges and anticipated totals with Peppol formulae.
Partial response, multiple responses, ignored cancellation, VMI consignment auto-orders, free-text items and substitution.

known_omissions: ICC Incoterms 2020 official text was not fetched; UBL only cites CIF, FOB and EXW as example delivery-term alignments
United States UCC Article 2 and FAR/DFARS federal purchase orders were not independently retrieved as primary sources
ASC X12 850/855 TR3 content is membership-gated; North American EDI is an alignment gap rather than a canonical node
UN/CEFACT Buyer's Order CCL / SCRDM was not fetched beyond EDIFACT ORDERS D.99B
Standing, rush, subscription and digital-goods or SaaS order semantics lack first-party coverage here
Islamic financing purchase instruments and letter-of-credit specific order clauses are not modelled
Line-level cancellation as a first-class document distinct from Order Change is not specified by the cited UBL process
National commercial-books retention periods (often five to ten years) are jurisdiction-specific and not enumerated
GDPR and other privacy statutes are not cited; only the presence of contact personal data on Peppol/UBL parties is sourced
conflicts: UN/EDIFACT document-name 105 Purchase Order is an internal enterprise document, while UBL alternative business term Purchase Order and common commercial usage mean the exchanged buyer-to-seller Order (typically code 220). This model follows the exchanged-commitment sense and maps 105 to originator requisition.

CISG art. 18: silence or inactivity is not in itself acceptance, but some courts give effect to commercial letters of confirmation where a usage exists under art. 9. Adopters must record which rule they apply.

Peppol dates shall not include timezone information, while this Dimension requires RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset; date-only source values must be normalised, not treated as already conformant.
UBL DocumentCurrencyCode is optional on Order; Peppol T01 makes it fatal-mandatory.
Peppol states TAX on orders is informative and does not affect terms of trade; some tax administrations may still treat a stated VAT amount as a representation. Do not claim tax-document status.
UBL full Order Response replaces the entire order state; Peppol also allows partial acceptance and multiple responses for one order. Both patterns must be recorded rather than collapsed.
ISO/IEC 19845 has frozen earlier UBL versions; OASIS UBL 2.4 is the OASIS Standard used here and is not automatically the ISO edition.
Peppol Ordering does not mandate eSignature; UBL defines a signature extension. Unsigned orders can be valid in Peppol and still lack non-repudiation evidence.
regional_assumptions: Peppol BIS Ordering is written for EU and EEA public eProcurement and B2B/B2G; it is an alignment, not a global mandate.
CISG applies to international sales of goods between contracting states and not automatically to services-only orders or to states that reserved Part II.
VAT, GST and sales-tax treatment of estimated tax on orders is regime-specific.
UN/EDIFACT ORDERS remains widely used in global retail and manufacturing independently of Peppol.
Public-sector buyers may be subject to EU procurement directives when using this BIS, as Peppol itself warns.
adversarial_checks: Do not treat the seller sales-order identifier as the purchase-order identity.
Do not treat an internal requisition or EDIFACT 105 document as the exchanged buyer-to-seller order.
Do not claim CISG governs a services-only purchase order without evidence that the applicable law so provides.
Do not treat silent non-response as acceptance unless a sourced practice or usage is recorded.
Do not use issue date, delivery date or tax period as an identifier.
Do not claim UBL or Peppol conformance unless the cited XSD and fatal business rules were actually evaluated.
Do not collapse despatch advice, invoice or payment into this model because they carry an order reference.
Do not treat cancellation as deletion of the retained original data message.
Do not assume accept-with-change is allowed without a prior agreement on how buyer assent is obtained.
